title: Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
summary: Outlier detection for interval-valued data has lacked an explanation layer. The paper derives closed-form Shapley values and a Shapley interaction index for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance under the IMCD estimator, decomposing outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. On the Cars and Spotify datasets it illustrates variable-level explanations and flags outliers consistent with domain knowledge.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The AIDA repository is a complete, self-contained R package: it ships the intCars.rda data, the IMCD estimator (R/IMCD.r), farness transform (R/farness.r), outlier flagging (R/int_outliers.r), and two vignettes (IMCD_examples.Rmd, Shapley_examples.Rmd) plus executed scripts in inst/doc/ that perform exactly the Cars analysis behind C1-C6 (reweighted IMCD with ~75% subset, 0.9 farness cutoff, Shapley barplot of the six largest distances). No weights, no downloads and no dead frameworks: the only needs are an R runtime and CRAN dependencies.
est_runtime: ~20-30 min: ~10-15 min to install R (if absent) and compile/install AIDA + CRAN deps, ~1-2 min to run the Cars IMCD + farness + Shapley vignette chunk
blockers: This is an R package, not Python: requires installing R plus CRAN dependencies (MAINT.Data, rrcov/robustbase, ggplot2, etc.), which is the bulk of the setup time
MAINT.Data is pinned at version 2.8.0 in the paper; newer CRAN versions may change the Cars import path slightly
IMCD subset selection is stochastic: reaching exactly the five named flags may require fixing the seed / repeating the random subset draw
Nothing renders offline: vignette figures need ggplot2 and the package built/installed (R CMD INSTALL) before the .Rmd will knit

approach: The AIDA repository is an R package, but the sandbox can only execute Python/pip/git, so the plan uses the shipped AIDA sources and vignettes as the executable specification and ports only the tiny Cars pipeline to Python. We read data/intCars.rda with pyreadr/rdata, extract the interval bounds and car labels, then port the reweighted IMCD, farness transform, squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and closed-form Shapley/interaction formulas line-by-line from R/IMCD.r, R/farness.r, R/int_distances.r, and R/Shapley.r. The primary target is C1: reproduce the five Figure 1 outlier labels with h=20, farness cutoff 0.9, and strict score>0.9 flagging. The same fit is reused for the Figure 2a top-six and Figure 3 Shapley diagnostics. C2-C6 are recorded in results/metrics.json as intermediate checks rather than separate experiments.
steps: Use Python to ensure third_party/AIDA exists; if not, run git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catarinaploureiro/AIDA.git third_party/AIDA. Do not modify author files.
Install Python dependencies needed for parsing RData: pip install pyreadr rdata; keep preinstalled numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib.

Inspect third_party/AIDA/data/intCars.rda from Python. First try pyreadr; if the intData S4 object is not directly convertible, use rdata to recursively dump object classes and attributes and locate slots LowerBounds, UpperBounds, Centers, Ranges, and Class/labels. Use man/ and R/intData_class.r to identify slot names.

Build the Cars matrix as n=27, p=4 lower/upper arrays with car-model labels. Confirm the four variables are lnPrice, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, and Acceleration; if Price is not already logged, apply natural log to both Price bounds and rename to lnPrice. Drop only the class variable from distance computations.
Compute interval centers c=(a+b)/2 and ranges r=b-a for the four variables. Assert finite values, positive ranges, and no accidental extra variables.
Port the symbolic covariance construction from R/int_cov.r using the Uniform[-1,1] latent moments; verify the 4x4 covariance matrix is symmetric positive definite on the full data.

Implement IMCD in src/imcd.py: for each random start draw h=20 observations, compute symbolic covariance determinant, perform concentration C-steps retaining the h smallest robust distances, and keep the subset with the smallest determinant. Use five seed blocks of 2000 starts and select the best determinant; verify determinant stability across blocks.

Reweight the best IMCD fit: compute farness scores for all 27 observations using the current center/covariance, retain observations with score <= 0.9, recompute the robust barycenter and covariance, and iterate until the retained set is stable. Record the initial h subset size and final reweighted inlier count.

Port the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance from R/int_distances.r and compute distances and farness scores for all 27 Cars observations. Assert all distances and scores are finite and farness scores lie in [0,1].

Flag observations with farness score strictly greater than 0.9. Record the flagged labels in descending squared-distance order. Compare the count to 5 and the labels to MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, and HondaNSK.

Compute Shapley values for all observations using the closed-form expression ported from R/Shapley.r. For Cars set Psi=0 and cross center-range terms to zero per the symmetric uniform assumption. Check that sum_j phi_j equals the squared distance to numerical tolerance 1e-8.
Select the six observations with the largest squared distances, as in Figure 2a, regardless of outlier flag. Confirm the set contains the five expected outliers and Bmwserie7.
Compute the Shapley interaction matrix from Equations (10)-(12), setting diagonal terms so each row sums to that observation's Shapley value. Produce the Ferrari interaction tile data for Figure 3b.

Generate results/figures/cars_farness_outliers.png, cars_shapley_top6.png, cars_center_range_decomp.png, and ferrari_interaction_tile.png. Plot expected versus computed labels where useful for debugging.

Write results/metrics.json with a claim-level section for C1-C6 plus diagnostic arrays: car labels, distances, farness scores, flagged labels, top-six labels/order, h and h-percent, final reweighted count, Shapley efficiency errors, and maximum absolute cross center-range term.
Run python reproduce.py for the full result and verify metrics.json contains C1 count/labels and all intermediate checks. Keep the full run deterministic with the configured seed.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load intCars and assert shape 27x4, compute centers/ranges, fit IMCD with h=20 and 50 random starts for one seed block, compute distances and farness scores, and run Shapley values for the first observation. Assert finite outputs, covariance determinant >0, and Shapley efficiency error <1e-8. Write results/smoke.json and exit without making full figures. Target runtime <90 seconds.
intermediate_checks: Dataset check: intCars has exactly 27 rows, 4 interval variables, and labels including the five expected car names; class labels are present but excluded from distances.
Preprocessing check: lnPrice lower/upper bounds are on log scale; EngCap, Top Speed, Acceleration are untouched; no extra standardization is applied.
Geometry check: all ranges positive; centers/ranges finite; symbolic covariance symmetric positive definite; condition number below 1e12.
Subset check: h=20, h/n=74.07%, reported as approximately 75%; final reweighted inlier count at score<=0.9 is recorded separately.
IMCD stability check: best covariance determinant agrees across five independent seed blocks to relative tolerance 1e-6; if not, increase starts before proceeding.
Distance sanity check: a classical non-robust interval Mahalanobis baseline should rank the same suspected outliers near the top; large disagreement signals an IMCD/porting bug.
Farness check: all scores in [0,1], values around the 0.9 cutoff are printed with labels so a borderline flag is visible.
C1 check: flagged count must be 5 for exact label match, and within 2 observations for the tolerance-based claim.
C3/C10 check: top six by descending squared distance must include the five expected outliers plus Bmwserie7, with Bmwserie7 present even if not flagged.
Shapley efficiency check: for every observation, |sum(phi)-distance| <= 1e-8.
C6 check: maximum absolute cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution is <= 1e-10 for all Cars observations.
Interaction check: for Ferrari, row sums of the interaction matrix equal the Shapley values to tolerance 1e-8.
budget_plan: Total ~25 minutes. Setup 6-8 min: git clone and pip install pyreadr/rdata plus data introspection. Smoke 1-2 min: 50-start IMCD and one-observation Shapley check. Full fit 6-8 min: five seed blocks of 2000 starts on 27x20 subsets, reweighting, Shapley values and interactions. Figures/metrics 2-3 min. Reserve 4-5 min for debugging S4 extraction or a borderline farness flag; if IMCD starts are slow, reduce to 1000 starts per block only after confirming determinant stability.

    7| c_step <- function(z,m,data){

    9|     d2 <- IMah_dist(data=data,z=z)
   10|     updated_z <- rep(0,length(z))
   11|     updated_z[order(d2)[1:m]] <- 1

"""Load the AIDA intCars.rda data file (R data with an S4 intData object).

The intData S4 object holds LowerBounds/UpperBounds-derived Centers and Ranges
slots, the latent case ("U_id_symmetric"), latent parameters (delta = 1/12),
variable names and observation names.  We read it with the `rdata` package
(pyreadr cannot parse S4 objects) and return plain numpy arrays.

Requirement IDs: R1, R2, R3.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from src import config


@dataclass
class IntData:
    """Plain-python mirror of the AIDA intData slots that matter here."""

    centers: np.ndarray          # (n, p) interval centers c = (a + b) / 2
    ranges: np.ndarray           # (n, p) interval ranges r = b - a
    obs_names: list[str]
    var_names: list[str]
    latent_case: str
    latent_param: list
    n_obs: int
    n_vars: int
    classes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    lower_bounds: np.ndarray | None = None
    upper_bounds: np.ndarray | None = None


def _to_1d_str_array(x) -> list[str]:
    return [str(v) for v in np.asarray(x).ravel()]


def load_intcars(path=None) -> IntData:
    """Load data/intCars.rda and return an IntData with centers/ranges."""
    import rdata

    path = config.DATA_FILE if path is None else path
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        parsed = rdata.parser.parse_file(str(path))
        converted = rdata.conversion.convert(parsed)
    cars = converted["intCars"]
    intd = cars["intData"]
    slots = vars(intd)

    centers = np.asarray(slots["Centers"], dtype=float)
    ranges = np.asarray(slots["Ranges"], dtype=float)
    obs_names = _to_1d_str_array(slots["ObsNames"])
    var_names = _to_1d_str_array(slots["VarNames"])
    latent_case = str(np.asarray(slots["LatentCase"]).ravel()[0])
    latent_param = [np.asarray(x, dtype=float).ravel() for x in slots["LatentParam"]]
    n_obs = int(np.asarray(slots["NObs"]).ravel()[0])
    n_vars = int(np.asarray(slots["NIVar"]).ravel()[0])

    # class variable (plotting only) from the microdata frame
    micro = cars["microdata"]
    if isinstance(micro, pd.DataFrame) and "class" in micro.columns:
        classes = [str(v) for v in micro["class"].tolist()]
        if isinstance(micro.index, pd.Index):
            micro_names = [str(v) for v in micro.index.tolist()]
            if micro_names != obs_names:
                # align classes to intData order
                classes = [
                    str(micro.loc[micro.index[micro_names.index(n)], "class"])
                    for n in obs_names
                ]
    else:
        classes = ["unknown"] * n_obs

    out = IntData(
        centers=centers,
        ranges=ranges,
        obs_names=obs_names,
        var_names=var_names,
        latent_case=latent_case,
        latent_param=latent_param,
        n_obs=n_obs,
        n_vars=n_vars,
        classes=classes,
    )

    # --- dataset-level assertions (R3, C2) -----------------------------------
    assert out.n_obs == config.EXPECTED_N_OBS, out.n_obs
    assert out.n_vars == config.EXPECTED_N_VARS, out.n_vars
    assert out.centers.shape == (out.n_obs, out.n_vars)
    assert out.ranges.shape == (out.n_obs, out.n_vars)
    assert list(out.var_names) == config.EXPECTED_VAR_NAMES, out.var_names
    assert latent_case == "U_id_symmetric"
    delta = float(latent_param[0][0])
    assert abs(delta - config.DELTA_UNIFORM) < 1e-12, delta
    for nm in config.EXPECTED_OUTLIERS + ["Bmwserie7"]:
        assert nm in obs_names, nm

    # --- preprocessing check (R2): lnPrice already on log scale -------------
    # If the stored centers equal log((LB+UB)/2) up to rounding the bounds are
    # logged; verify a couple of known values instead of re-deriving.
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(out.centers)) and np.all(np.isfinite(out.ranges))
    assert np.all(out.ranges > 0), "all interval ranges must be positive"
    # lnPrice bounds in the raw MAINT.Data are ~28000-140000; logged centers are
    # ~9.8-12.2.  Guard against accidentally re-logging or missing the log.
    lp = out.centers[:, 0]
    assert 8.0 < lp.min() and lp.max() < 13.0, (
        "lnPrice centers are not on the natural-log scale: "
        f"[{lp.min():.3f}, {lp.max():.3f}]"
    )
    return out


def reconstruct_bounds(data: IntData):
    """c +/- r/2 lower/upper bounds (not used in the fit; for reporting)."""
    lo = data.centers - data.ranges / 2.0
    hi = data.centers + data.ranges / 2.0
    return lo, hi

    d2(x)   = (c - mu_C)' S^{-1} (c - mu_C) + delta (r - mu_R)' S^{-1} (r - mu_R)

"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from src import config


def int_mean_z(z: np.ndarray, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Column means of the rows of X selected by the binary mask z (AIDA int_mean_z)."""

    """Symbolic covariance of the barycenter on the subset z (AIDA int_cov_z).

    sigma_b = 1/m * sum_h z_h c_h c_h' - mu_c mu_c'
            + delta * (1/m * sum_h z_h r_h r_h' - mu_r mu_r')
    """
    idx = np.flatnonzero(z)
    m = idx.size
    if m == 0:
        raise ValueError("empty subset")
    mu_c = C[idx].mean(axis=0)
    mu_r = R[idx].mean(axis=0)
    sigma_cc = (C[idx].T @ C[idx]) / m - np.outer(mu_c, mu_c)
    sigma_rr = (R[idx].T @ R[idx]) / m - np.outer(mu_r, mu_r)
    return sigma_cc + delta * sigma_rr


def imah_dist(S: np.ndarray, mu_c: np.ndarray, mu_r: np.ndarray,
              C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distances for all observations.

    AIDA IMah_dist: d2 = (c - mu_c)' S^{-1} (c - mu_c)
                         + delta (r - mu_r)' S^{-1} (r - mu_r)
    Computed via solve() to avoid explicitly forming the inverse.
    """
    dC = C - mu_c
    dR = R - mu_r
    L = np.linalg.cholesky(S)
    yC = np.linalg.solve_triangular(L, dC.T, lower=True)
    yR = np.linalg.solve_triangular(L, dR.T, lower=True)
    d2_c = np.einsum("ij,ij->j", yC, yC)
    d2_r = np.einsum("ij,ij->j", yR, yR)
    return d2_c + delta * d2_r


def safe_solve_cov(S: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Plain inverse with fallback to the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse.

    AIDA safe_solve_cov: try solve(), on failure use ginv().  For the tiny,
    well-conditioned Cars covariance the plain inverse always succeeds.
    """
    try:
        return np.linalg.inv(S)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.linalg.pinv(S)

"""AIDA farness() and int_outliers() ported to Python (R/farness.r, R/int_outliers.r).

Pipeline (R6): squared robust distances -> median/MAD standardization ->
robust Yeo-Johnson (cellWise transfo) -> second median/MAD standardization ->
Normal-CDF scoring.  Requirement R7: probs > cutoff flags outliers.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import norm

from src import config
from src.farness_yj import r_median, r_mad, transfo_yj_column, transfo_transformback_yj


def farness(dist: np.ndarray, cutoff_value: float | None = None):
    """AIDA farness(): farness outlier probabilities for squared distances.

    Returns (probs, cutoff_dist, info).  `cutoff_dist` is the cutoff on the
    original distance scale (None when cutoff_value is None).
    """
    dist = np.asarray(dist, dtype=float)
    indnz = np.flatnonzero(dist > config.FARNESS_INDNZ_EPS)
    farnz = dist[indnz]

    farloc = r_median(farnz)
    farsca = r_mad(farnz)
    if farsca < config.FARNESS_INDNZ_EPS:
        farsca = float(np.std(farnz, ddof=1))
    sfar = (farnz - farloc) / farsca

    xt, est = transfo_yj_column(sfar)

    tfarloc = r_median(xt)
    tfarsca = r_mad(xt)
    zt = (xt - tfarloc) / tfarsca

    probs = np.zeros(dist.size)
    probs[indnz] = norm.cdf(zt)

    cutoff_dist = None
    if cutoff_value is not None:
        if not (0.0 <= cutoff_value <= 1.0):
            raise ValueError("cutoff_value must be between 0 and 1")
        cut = norm.ppf(cutoff_value)
        cut = cut * tfarsca + tfarloc
        cut = transfo_transformback_yj(cut, est["lambdahat_rew"])
        cut = cut * farsca + farloc
        cutoff_dist = float(cut)

    info = {
        "farloc": farloc, "farsca": farsca,
        "tfarloc": tfarloc, "tfarsca": tfarsca,
        "lambdahat_raw": est["lambdahat_raw"],
        "lambdahat_rew": est["lambdahat_rew"],
    }
    return probs, cutoff_dist, info


def int_outliers(robust_dist: np.ndarray, cutoff_lvl: float = config.FARNESS_CUTOFF):
    """AIDA int_outliers(cutoff='farness', cutoff_lvl=0.9).

    Returns (is_outlier, probs, cutoff_dist, info): is_outlier[i] is True iff
    the farness probability of observation i strictly exceeds cutoff_lvl.
    """
    probs, cutoff_dist, info = farness(robust_dist, cutoff_value=cutoff_lvl)
    is_outlier = probs > cutoff_lvl
    return is_outlier, probs, cutoff_dist, info

"""AIDA IMCD estimator ported to Python (R/IMCD.r).

Algorithm (smallIMCD path, n <= 600):
  1. draw_z: random (p+1)-subset (extended while the symbolic covariance is
     singular), then keep the m observations closest to that fit (A1 seed).
  2. 500 initial subsets -> one c_step each -> keep the 10 with smallest
     determinant (pick10) -> full C-step convergence (it=0) of those 10 ->
     keep the overall minimum-determinant subset.
  3. Farness reweighting at cutoff 0.9 (single pass, as current AIDA):
     w = farness(raw robust d2) <= 0.9, refit mean/cov on w.

Multiple master seed blocks are run for determinism (R is runif()-seed
dependent); the block with the global minimum raw determinant drives the
primary result, and per-seed flags are recorded as a stability check.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from src import config
from src.farness import farness
from src.interval_ops import int_cov_z, int_mean_z, imah_dist


def _top_m_mask(d2: np.ndarray, m: int) -> np.ndarray:
    order = np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")
    z = np.zeros(d2.size, dtype=int)
    z[order[:m]] = 1
    return z


def draw_z(rng: np.random.Generator, m: int, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray,
           delta: float, p: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """AIDA draw_z: initial h-subset around a random (p+1)-subset fit."""
    n = C.shape[0]
    j = rng.choice(n, size=p + 1, replace=False)
    z = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)
    z[j] = 1
    sigma = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    while np.linalg.det(sigma) == 0.0 and len(j) < n - 1:
        extra = int(rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(~z.astype(bool))))
        j = np.append(j, extra)
        z = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)
        z[j] = 1
        sigma = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    mu_c = int_mean_z(z, C)
    mu_r = int_mean_z(z, R)
    d2 = imah_dist(sigma, mu_c, mu_r, C, R, delta)
    return _top_m_mask(d2, m)


def c_step(z: np.ndarray, m: int, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """AIDA c_step: refit on z, keep the m nearest, refit on the new subset."""
    mu_c = int_mean_z(z, C)
    mu_r = int_mean_z(z, R)
    sigma = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    d2 = imah_dist(sigma, mu_c, mu_r, C, R, delta)
    updated_z = _top_m_mask(d2, m)
    S = int_cov_z(updated_z, C, R, delta)
    means_c = int_mean_z(updated_z, C)
    means_r = int_mean_z(updated_z, R)
    return S, means_c, means_r, updated_z, d2


def step_it(z: np.ndarray, m: int, it: int, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray,
            delta: float, max_iter: int = config.C_STEP_MAX_ITER):
    """AIDA step_it: apply c_step `it` times (it=0 -> until no improvement)."""
    S, means_c, means_r, updated_z, _ = c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
    if it == 0:
        det_old = np.inf
        det_new = float(np.linalg.det(S))
        n_iter = 0
        while det_old > det_new > 0 and n_iter < max_iter:
            S, means_c, means_r, updated_z, _ = c_step(updated_z, m, C, R, delta)
            det_old = det_new
            det_new = float(np.linalg.det(S))
            n_iter += 1
    d2 = imah_dist(S, means_c, means_r, C, R, delta)
    return S, means_c, means_r, updated_z, d2


def _pick10(z_all: np.ndarray, m: int, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """AIDA pick10: rank the 500 initial subsets by 1-c_step determinant."""
    n_starts = z_all.shape[1]
    dets = np.empty(n_starts)
    for i in range(n_starts):
        S = c_step(z_all[:, i], m, C, R, delta)[0]
        dets[i] = np.linalg.det(S)
    i10 = np.argsort(dets, kind="stable")[:10]
    return z_all[:, i10], dets[i10]


def smallIMCD(rng: np.random.Generator, m: int, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray,
              delta: float, n_starts: int = config.IMCD_N_STARTS, p: int = None):
    """AIDA smallIMCD: best converged subset over 500 random starts."""
    if p is None:
        p = C.shape[1]
    z_all = np.column_stack(
        [draw_z(rng, m, C, R, delta, p) for _ in range(n_starts)])
    z10, _ = _pick10(z_all, m, C, R, delta)
    res10 = [step_it(z10[:, i], m, 0, C, R, delta) for i in range(z10.shape[1])]
    dets10 = np.array([np.linalg.det(r[0]) for r in res10])
    best = res10[int(np.argmin(dets10))]
    out = {
        "S": best[0], "mu_c": best[1], "mu_r": best[2], "z": best[3],
        "robust_dist": best[4], "det": float(np.linalg.det(best[0])),
    }
    return out


def _reweight(raw: dict, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float,
              cutoff: float):
    """AIDA IMCD farness reweighting: single reweighting pass at `cutoff`."""
    d2_raw = raw["robust_dist"]
    probs_raw, _, info_raw = farness(d2_raw, cutoff_value=cutoff)
    w = (probs_raw <= cutoff).astype(int)
    if int(w.sum()) > C.shape[1]:
        z = w
    else:  # degenerate keep (should not happen for Cars)
        z = raw["z"]
    mu_c = int_mean_z(z, C)
    mu_r = int_mean_z(z, R)
    S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    d2 = imah_dist(S, mu_c, mu_r, C, R, delta)
    return {
        "z": z, "S": S, "mu_c": mu_c, "mu_r": mu_r, "robust_dist": d2,
        "det": float(np.linalg.det(S)),
        "probs_raw": probs_raw, "raw_subset_size": int(raw["z"].sum()),
        "kept_size": int(z.sum()), "raw_det": raw["det"],
        "raw_subset": raw["z"], "info_raw": info_raw,
    }


def imcd(C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float, m: int,
         cutoff: float = config.FARNESS_CUTOFF,
         n_starts: int = config.IMCD_N_STARTS,
         n_seeds: int = config.IMCD_N_SEEDS,
         base_seed: int = config.RNG_SEED):
    """Full AIDA IMCD with multi-seed restart for determinism.

    Returns the best-seed reweighted fit plus per-seed stability records.
    """
    p = C.shape[1]
    seeds = [base_seed + s for s in range(n_seeds)]

            "seed": sd, "raw_det": rew["raw_det"], "final_det": rew["det"],

"""Closed-form Shapley values / decomposition / interaction for interval data.

Direct ports of AIDA R/Shapley.r for the "U_id_symmetric" latent case
(Psi = 0, cross centers-ranges terms identically zero):

  phi_j(x)      = c0_j (S^{-1} c0)_j + delta * r0_j (S^{-1} r0)_j
  Centers_j     = c0_j (S^{-1} c0)_j
  Ranges_j      = delta * r0_j (S^{-1} r0)_j
  inter_{jk}    = 2 c0_j c0_k Sinv_{jk} + 2 delta r0_j r0_k Sinv_{jk}
  Phi_{jk}      = inter_{jk} - delta_{jk} phi_j(x)   (row sums equal phi)

Requirement IDs: R8, R9, R11.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from src.interval_ops import safe_solve_cov


def int_shapley(C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, mu_c: np.ndarray, mu_r: np.ndarray,
                S: np.ndarray, delta: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """AIDA int_Shapley for U_id_symmetric: (n, p) additive contributions."""
    Sinv = safe_solve_cov(S)
    dC = C - mu_c
    dR = R - mu_r
    tC = Sinv @ dC.T
    tR = Sinv @ dR.T
    phi = dC * tC.T + delta * dR * tR.T
    return phi


def int_shapley_decomp(C, R, mu_c, mu_r, S, delta):
    """AIDA int_Shapley_decomp for U_id_symmetric -> (centers, ranges, cross)."""
    Sinv = safe_solve_cov(S)
    dC = C - mu_c
    dR = R - mu_r
    centers = dC * (Sinv @ dC.T).T
    ranges = delta * dR * (Sinv @ dR.T).T
    cross = np.zeros_like(centers)  # U_id_symmetric: no cross term (R9)
    return centers, ranges, cross


def int_shapley_interaction(x_c: np.ndarray, x_r: np.ndarray, mu_c: np.ndarray,
                            mu_r: np.ndarray, S: np.ndarray, delta: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """AIDA int_Shapley_interaction (U_id_symmetric), diagonal set by row sums."""
    Sinv = safe_solve_cov(S)
    c0 = x_c - mu_c
    r0 = x_r - mu_r
    inter = 2.0 * np.outer(c0, c0) * Sinv + 2.0 * delta * np.outer(r0, r0) * Sinv
    phi = c0 * (Sinv @ c0) + delta * r0 * (Sinv @ r0)
    Phi = inter - np.diag(phi)
    return Phi


def cross_term_max_abs(C, R, mu_c, mu_r, S, delta):
    """Maximum |cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution| over observations.

    For the symmetric uniform latent case the U_id cross term is evaluated
    with E[U] = 0 (Psi = 0), which makes it identically zero.
    """
    _, _, cross = int_shapley_decomp(C, R, mu_c, mu_r, S, delta)
    return float(np.max(np.abs(cross)))

def fig3b_interaction_tile(var_names, Phi, obs_name, path):

    for i in range(Phi.shape[0]):

    ax.set_title(f"Cars: Shapley interactions ({obs_name})")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)

"""End-to-end Cars pipeline: data -> IMCD -> farness flags -> Shapley -> outputs."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from src import config
from src.farness import int_outliers
from src.imcd import imcd
from src.interval_ops import int_cov_z, int_mean_z, imah_dist
from src.plots import (fig1_farness_outliers, fig2a_shapley_top6,
                       fig3a_center_range_decomp, fig3b_interaction_tile)
from src.rdata_loader import load_intcars
from src.shapley import (cross_term_max_abs, int_shapley,
                         int_shapley_decomp, int_shapley_interaction)


def run_pipeline(n_starts: int, n_seeds: int, make_figures: bool,
                 results_dir: Path, figures_dir: Path, tag: str = "full"):
    """Run the Cars reproduction and return a results dict."""
    t0 = time.time()
    data = load_intcars()
    C, R = data.centers, data.ranges
    n, p = C.shape
    delta = config.DELTA_UNIFORM
    obs_names = data.obs_names

    # --- R4: reweighted IMCD with ~75% subset, farness cutoff 0.9 ----------
    m = int(np.floor(config.H_SUBSET_FRACTION * n))
    fit = imcd(C, R, delta, m, cutoff=config.FARNESS_CUTOFF,
               n_starts=n_starts, n_seeds=n_seeds, base_seed=config.RNG_SEED)
    d2 = fit["robust_dist"]  # reweighted squared robust distances

    # --- R7/C1: flag outliers with farness cutoff 0.9 ----------------------
    is_outlier, probs, cutoff_dist, finfo = int_outliers(
        d2, cutoff_lvl=config.FARNESS_CUTOFF)
    flag_idx = np.flatnonzero(is_outlier)
    flagged_names = [obs_names[i] for i in flag_idx]
    # descending squared-distance order (R12)
    flag_idx = flag_idx[np.argsort(-d2[flag_idx], kind="stable")]
    flagged_ordered = [obs_names[i] for i in flag_idx]

    # --- R8/R9: Shapley values + decomposition + efficiency ----------------
    shapley = int_shapley(C, R, fit["mu_c"], fit["mu_r"], fit["S"], delta)
    centers, ranges, cross = int_shapley_decomp(
        C, R, fit["mu_c"], fit["mu_r"], fit["S"], delta)
    eff_err = np.abs(shapley.sum(axis=1) - d2)
    cross_max = cross_term_max_abs(C, R, fit["mu_c"], fit["mu_r"], fit["S"], delta)

    # --- C3/R10: six largest squared distances (regardless of flag) --------
    top_idx = np.argsort(-d2, kind="stable")[:config.TOP_K]
    top_names = [obs_names[i] for i in top_idx]

    # --- R11: Ferrari interaction tile data --------------------------------
    ferr_idx = obs_names.index(config.INTERACTION_TARGET)
    Phi = int_shapley_interaction(C[ferr_idx], R[ferr_idx], fit["mu_c"],
                                  fit["mu_r"], fit["S"], delta)
    phi_ferr = shapley[ferr_idx]
    inter_row_err = np.abs(Phi.sum(axis=1) - phi_ferr)

    # --- classical non-robust baseline (sanity check) ----------------------
    z_all = np.ones(n, dtype=int)
    mu_c_c = int_mean_z(z_all, C)
    mu_r_c = int_mean_z(z_all, R)
    S_c = int_cov_z(z_all, C, R, delta)
    d2_classical = imah_dist(S_c, mu_c_c, mu_r_c, C, R, delta)

    # per-seed stability detail
    for rec in fit["per_seed"]:
        rec["raw_subset_names"] = [obs_names[i] for i in np.flatnonzero(
            fit["raw_subset"] == 1)] if False else None

    res = {
        "obs_names": obs_names,
        "var_names": data.var_names,
        "classes": data.classes,
        "n_obs": n, "n_vars": p,
        "h": m, "h_percent": 100.0 * m / n,
        "farness_cutoff": config.FARNESS_CUTOFF,
        "d2": d2, "probs": probs, "cutoff_dist": cutoff_dist,
        "flagged_names": flagged_names,
        "flagged_ordered": flagged_ordered,
        "n_flagged": len(flagged_names),
        "is_outlier": is_outlier,
        "top6_names": top_names,
        "shapley": shapley, "centers": centers, "ranges": ranges,
        "eff_err_max": float(eff_err.max()),
        "cross_max": cross_max,
        "interaction_ferrari": Phi,
        "interaction_row_err_max": float(inter_row_err.max()),
        "fit": fit, "farness_info": finfo,
        "d2_classical": d2_classical,
        "runtime_s": time.time() - t0,
        "n_starts": n_starts, "n_seeds": n_seeds,
    }

    # --- figures -----------------------------------------------------------
    if make_figures:
        figures_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fig1 = figures_dir / "cars_farness_outliers.png"
        fig2 = figures_dir / "cars_shapley_top6.png"
        fig3 = figures_dir / "cars_center_range_decomp.png"
        fig4 = figures_dir / "ferrari_interaction_tile.png"
        fig1_farness_outliers(obs_names, d2, cutoff_dist, is_outlier, fig1)
        fig2a_shapley_top6(obs_names, shapley, d2, cutoff_dist, fig2, top_idx)
        fig3a_center_range_decomp(obs_names, centers, ranges, d2, fig3, top_idx)
        fig3b_interaction_tile(data.var_names, Phi, config.INTERACTION_TARGET, fig4)
        res["figures"] = [str(fig1), str(fig2), str(fig3), str(fig4)]
    return res

"""Assemble the Cars reproduction diagnostics into results/metrics.json.

Every value below is computed from the data by the pipeline; the paper's
stated values are never referenced (the expected outlier labels live in
config only for an independent match check).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from src import config


def build_metrics(res: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert the pipeline result into the metrics.json document."""
    obs_names = res["obs_names"]
    expected = config.EXPECTED_OUTLIERS
    flagged = res["flagged_ordered"]
    top6 = res["top6_names"]
    match_labels = set(flagged) == set(expected)
    match_top6 = all(nm in top6 for nm in expected + ["Bmwserie7"])

    # per-observation diagnostics
    d2 = res["d2"]
    probs = res["probs"]
    is_out = res["is_outlier"]
    order = np.argsort(-d2, kind="stable")
    per_obs = [
        {
            "name": obs_names[i],
            "d2": float(d2[i]),
            "farness_prob": float(probs[i]),
            "is_outlier": bool(is_out[i]),
            "d2_classical": float(res["d2_classical"][i]),
        }
        for i in order
    ]

    metrics = {
        "metric": "number of observations flagged as outliers",
        "value": int(res["n_flagged"]),
        "dataset": "Cars (MAINT.Data), 27 observations x 4 interval variables",
        "split": "full dataset",
        "config": {
            "transform": "lnPrice (natural log of Price bounds); EngCap, "
                         "Top Speed, Acceleration unchanged",
            "latent_microdata": "independent Uniform[-1,1]; delta=1/12; "
                                "U_id_symmetric; Psi=0",
            "estimator": "reweighted IMCD (AIDA smallIMCD port)",
            "h_subset_size": int(res["h"]),
            "h_percent": round(res["h_percent"], 4),
            "farness_cutoff": float(res["farness_cutoff"]),
            "flag_rule": "farness probability > 0.9",
            "imcd_n_starts_per_seed": int(res["n_starts"]),
            "imcd_n_seed_blocks": int(res["n_seeds"]),
            "rng_seed_base": config.RNG_SEED,
        },
        "notes": "R IMCD subset draws are runif-based and cannot be replayed "
                 "bit-for-bit in Python; determinism is obtained by running "
                 "multiple master seed blocks and taking the global minimum "
                 "raw covariance determinant (stability across blocks is "
                 "reported below).",
        "claims": {
            "C1": {
                "description": "number of observations flagged as outliers",
                "value": int(res["n_flagged"]),
                "flagged_labels_desc_distance": flagged,
                "matches_paper_labels": bool(match_labels),
            },
            "C2": {
                "description": "number of observations in dataset",
                "value": int(res["n_obs"]),
                "n_vars": int(res["n_vars"]),
                "var_names": list(res["var_names"]),
            },
            "C3": {
                "description": "number of observations shown in Shapley "
                               "barplot (largest squared distances)",
                "value": len(top6),
                "top6_labels_desc_distance": top6,
                "includes_Bmwserie7": bool("Bmwserie7" in top6),
                "matches_expected_top6": bool(match_top6),
            },
            "C4": {
                "description": "IMCD subset size as percent of observations "
                               "(h = floor(0.75 n); reweighted inliers too)",
                "value": round(res["h_percent"], 4),
                "final_reweighted_inlier_percent": round(
                    100.0 * res["fit"]["kept_size"] / res["n_obs"], 4),
            },
            "C5": {
                "description": "farness cutoff used to flag outliers",
                "value": float(res["farness_cutoff"]),
            },
            "C6": {
                "description": "cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution "
                               "(max absolute over observations)",
                "value": res["cross_max"],
                "tol": config.CROSS_TERM_ZERO_TOL,
            },
        },
        "diagnostics": {
            "farness_cutoff_on_distance_scale": res["cutoff_dist"],
            "lambdahat_raw_first_farness": res["fit"]["info_raw"]["lambdahat_raw"],
            "lambdahat_rew_first_farness": res["fit"]["info_raw"]["lambdahat_rew"],
            "lambdahat_raw_final_farness": res["farness_info"]["lambdahat_raw"],
            "lambdahat_rew_final_farness": res["farness_info"]["lambdahat_rew"],
            "imcd_raw_det": res["fit"]["raw_det"],
            "imcd_final_det": res["fit"]["det"],
            "imcd_kept_size": res["fit"]["kept_size"],
            "imcd_det_rel_spread_across_seeds": res["fit"]["det_rel_spread"],
            "shapley_efficiency_max_abs_error": res["eff_err_max"],
            "interaction_ferrari_row_sum_max_abs_error": res["interaction_row_err_max"],
            "interaction_ferrari_matrix": np.asarray(
                res["interaction_ferrari"]).tolist(),
            "per_seed": [
                {k: v for k, v in rec.items()} for rec in res["per_seed"]
            ],
            "per_observation_desc_distance": per_obs,
            "runtime_s": round(res["runtime_s"], 3),
        },
    }
    return metrics


def write_metrics(res: dict, path) -> dict:
    """Build and write metrics.json; return the document."""
    import json
    metrics = build_metrics(res)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(metrics, fh, indent=2, default=float)
    return metrics

"""Reproduce the Cars outlier-detection results of
"Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data" (arXiv:2606.26307).

Target claim C1: the 0.9-farness Cars analysis flags five observations as
outliers (MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK).

The authors' AIDA package (R) ships in ./repo and is used only as the
executable specification; the full pipeline is ported to Python:

  python reproduce.py            # full run -> results/metrics.json + figures
  python reproduce.py --smoke    # quick sanity run -> results/smoke.json
  python reproduce.py --search   # extended seed stability scan -> selected_config.json
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from src import config
from src.metrics import write_metrics
from src.pipeline import run_pipeline


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true",
                        help="quick reduced run writing results/smoke.json")
    parser.add_argument("--search", action="store_true",
                        help="extended seed-stability scan (separate from the "
                             "default run; writes selected_config.json)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    results_dir = ROOT / "results"
    figures_dir = results_dir / "figures"
    results_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if args.smoke:
        res = run_pipeline(n_starts=config.SMOKE_N_STARTS,
                           n_seeds=config.SMOKE_N_SEEDS,
                           make_figures=False,
                           results_dir=results_dir, figures_dir=figures_dir,
                           tag="smoke")
        smoke = {
            "n_obs": res["n_obs"], "n_vars": res["n_vars"],
            "h": res["h"], "h_percent": res["h_percent"],
            "n_flagged": res["n_flagged"],
            "flagged_ordered": res["flagged_ordered"],
            "shapley_efficiency_max_abs_error": res["eff_err_max"],
            "cross_max": res["cross_max"],
            "imcd_final_det": res["fit"]["det"],
            "ok": bool(res["n_obs"] == 27 and res["n_vars"] == 4
                       and res["fit"]["det"] > 0
                       and res["eff_err_max"] < config.SHAPLEY_EFFICIENCY_TOL
                       and res["n_flagged"] > 0),
        }
        with open(results_dir / "smoke.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(smoke, fh, indent=2)
        print("SMOKE:", json.dumps(smoke, indent=2))
        return

    if args.search:
        # Extended seed scan: more blocks, same protocol otherwise.  The
        # outcome only demonstrates stability; the default run already uses
        # the fixed protocol constants.
        n_blocks = 20
        res = run_pipeline(n_starts=config.IMCD_N_STARTS, n_seeds=n_blocks,
                           make_figures=False,
                           results_dir=results_dir, figures_dir=figures_dir,
                           tag="search")
        report = {
            "protocol": {
                "h": res["h"], "h_percent": res["h_percent"],
                "farness_cutoff": res["farness_cutoff"],
                "n_starts_per_seed": res["n_starts"],
                "base_seed": config.RNG_SEED,

args.summary: Reproduced the Cars outlier analysis of "Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data" (arXiv:2606.26307) in pure Python, using the authors' AIDA R package (shipped in ./repo) as the executable specification. The full pipeline was ported line-by-line: intCars.rda loading (27×4 interval data, lnPrice/EngCap/Top Speed/Acceleration, U_id_symmetric latent case with δ=1/12), the reweighted IMCD estimator (h=floor(0.75·27)=20, 500 random starts, C-step convergence, single farness reweighting at cutoff 0.9), the farness score transform (median/MAD → robust Yeo-Johnson via a faithful port of cellWise 2.5.3 transfo/YJr/reweightYJr → median/MAD → Normal CDF), the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and the closed-form Shapley values/decomposition/interaction (Ψ=0). TARGET CLAIM C1 REPRODUCED EXACTLY: exactly 5 observations flagged at the 0.9-farness cutoff — MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK (in descending squared-distance order, matching the paper). The result is seed-independent: all 5 deterministic IMCD seed blocks converge to the identical raw covariance determinant (relative spread 0.0) and identical flags. Supporting claims also verified and recorded in results/metrics.json: C2 (27 obs × 4 vars), C3 (top-6 distances = 5 outliers + Bmwserie7, matching Figure 2a), C4 (h=20 → 74.07% ≈ 75% subset; 21/27=77.78% reweighted inliers), C5 (cutoff 0.9, distance-scale cutoff ≈16.27), C6 (max |cross centers-ranges Shapley term| = 0.0 exactly), Shapley efficiency max error 3.6e-14, Ferrari interaction matrix row sums equal Shapley values. Clean re-run from a deleted results/ folder: exit 0 in ~14 s (limit 20 min), writing results/metrics.json and the four diagnostic figures. No scaling down: the complete protocol was implemented. summary: Reproduced the Cars outlier analysis of "Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data" (arXiv:2606.26307) in pure Python, using the authors' AIDA R package (shipped in ./repo) as the executable specification. The full pipeline was ported line-by-line: intCars.rda loading (27×4 interval data, lnPrice/EngCap/Top Speed/Acceleration, U_id_symmetric latent case with δ=1/12), the reweighted IMCD estimator (h=floor(0.75·27)=20, 500 random starts, C-step convergence, single farness reweighting at cutoff 0.9), the farness score transform (median/MAD → robust Yeo-Johnson via a faithful port of cellWise 2.5.3 transfo/YJr/reweightYJr → median/MAD → Normal CDF), the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and the closed-form Shapley values/decomposition/interaction (Ψ=0). TARGET CLAIM C1 REPRODUCED EXACTLY: exactly 5 observations flagged at the 0.9-farness cutoff — MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK (in descending squared-distance order, matching the paper). The result is seed-independent: all 5 deterministic IMCD seed blocks converge to the identical raw covariance determinant (relative spread 0.0) and identical flags. Supporting claims also verified and recorded in results/metrics.json: C2 (27 obs × 4 vars), C3 (top-6 distances = 5 outliers + Bmwserie7, matching Figure 2a), C4 (h=20 → 74.07% ≈ 75% subset; 21/27=77.78% reweighted inliers), C5 (cutoff 0.9, distance-scale cutoff ≈16.27), C6 (max |cross centers-ranges Shapley term| = 0.0 exactly), Shapley efficiency max error 3.6e-14, Ferrari interaction matrix row sums equal Shapley values. Clean re-run from a deleted results/ folder: exit 0 in ~14 s (limit 20 min), writing results/metrics.json and the four diagnostic figures. No scaling down: the complete protocol was implemented. Paper numbers were never copied into code; the expected labels exist only as an independent match check in config.

audit_summary: The clean re-run exited 0 in 8.8 s and wrote value 5, with exactly the paper's five outlier labels in descending squared-distance order and Bmwserie7 just below the 0.9 cutoff. All checkable requirements are met: h=20 (74.07%), cutoff 0.9, Shapley efficiency error 3.6e-14, zero cross center-range terms, and the required top-6 display including Bmwserie7. There is no evidence of hardcoded reported numbers; paper_numbers_found_in_code is empty, and the expected labels appear only as a match check. The run uses the full 27x4 Cars data and the IMCD + farness + Shapley pipeline, with no subset/epoch/repeat scaling. The main audit limitation is that the supplied source bundle contains only a matplotlib font cache, so code-level fidelity is inferred from the command ledger and detailed metrics rather than direct line-by-line source review.
